earnings.title: T-Mobile Delivers Strong Account and ARPA Growth, Translating into Industry-Leading Service Revenue, Profitability and EPS Growth
highlights: Net income of $3.5 billion grew 27% year-over-year, industry-leading growth
Diluted earnings per share (“EPS”) of $3.22 grew 34% year-over-year, industry-leading growth
Postpaid Average Revenue Per Account (“ARPA”) of $155.73 grew 4% year-over-year
Service revenues of $19.4 billion grew 6% year-over-year, industry-leading growth (1)
Postpaid service revenues of $16.3 billion grew 9% year-over-year, industry-leading growth

quotes.text: Q3 marked another strong quarter and is further proof that our winning formula of the best network, best value, and best experiences drives durable and profitable growth.

outlook: Postpaid net account additions are expected to be approximately 1.0 million, at the midpoint of the previous guide of 950 thousand to 1.05 million.
Effective tax rate is now expected to be between 24% and 25%, a decrease from prior guidance of between 25% and 26%.

Core Adjusted EBITDA, which is Adjusted EBITDA less lease revenues, is expected to be between $37.35 billion and $37.45 billion, an increase at the midpoint from prior guidance of $37.1 billion to $37.5 billion.

Net cash provided by operating activities, including net payments for UScellular merger-related costs, is now expected to be between $28.7 billion and $28.8 billion, an increase at the midpoint from prior guidance of $28.4 billion to $28.8 billion.

items.heading: We operate in a highly competitive industry. If we are unable to attract and retain customers, our business, financial condition, and operating results could be negatively affected.

We have experienced cyberattacks and may experience disruptions, data loss and other security breaches, whether directly or indirectly through third parties whose products and services we rely on in operating our business.

If we fail to adopt and deploy emerging network technologies in a timely and effective manner, our competitive position could erode, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and operating results.

If we fail to effectively execute our digital transformation and drive customer and employee adoption of emerging technologies, our competitive position and financial performance could be materially harmed.

We rely on highly skilled personnel throughout all levels of our business. Our business could be harmed if we are unable to retain or motivate key personnel, hire a sufficient number of qualified new personnel, or maintain our corporate culture.
System failures and business disruptions may prevent us from providing reliable service, which could materially and adversely affect our reputation and financial condition.
